# Windows external private-Ygg operator onboarding

This is an operator procedure for enrolling a Windows laptop as an external
private-Ygg transport participant for the Arbor cluster.

Codex cannot configure or inspect the Windows laptop from the current
execution environment. No Windows service, Yggdrasil identity, route, SSH
connection, or enrollment was verified while preparing this document. Values
marked as operator-supplied must come from the current accepted Arbor Registry
snapshot or another explicitly authoritative public-metadata export; do not
fill them from memory or invention.

## Scope and trust boundary

The laptop is an external/operator endpoint, not a NixOS host. The supported
Windows path is the upstream Yggdrasil MSI with a persistent static
configuration. The NixOS-only Arbor Network Manager/provider-socket mode is
not available on Windows in this repository.

The roles remain separate:

```text
accepted Arbor Registry records
        -> approved public peer metadata
        -> Windows Yggdrasil static configuration
        -> private transport
```

Yggdrasil supplies transport. Arbor Registry accepted state supplies
enrollment, identity, relationships, capabilities, and revocation. Discovery
or packet reachability never grants Arbor trust or administrative authority.
Do not add the laptop to an operator or deployment grant merely because it can
join the Yggdrasil network.

The NixOS participants retain the special runtime mode:
`site.networks.privateYggdrasil.networkManager.enable = true`. Their desired
peers are delivered through the Arbor provider socket and are not replaced by
this Windows procedure.

## Information required before installation

Obtain a current, signed or otherwise approved public metadata export from the
Arbor operator. It must identify the accepted snapshot/generation and digest,
expiration or revalidation time, and the approved records for:

- `r640-0`
- `desktoptoodle`
- `eVolver`
- the external laptop identity, if the Registry schema supports it

For every approved peer, copy only the public values required by the upstream
Yggdrasil configuration: hostname/label, Yggdrasil address, public key,
approved endpoint URI(s), and the exact `AllowedPublicKeys` set. Record the
source snapshot, generation, and digest beside the local configuration. Do
not invent an address, key, endpoint, peer relationship, or expiration.

The supplied laptop SSH keys are separate from the Yggdrasil identity. Both
remain valid operator credentials during this milestone:

- `laptopOperatorKeys / admin@toptoodle`
- `laptopOperatorKeys / phsilbert@gmail.com`

Only their public halves are represented in Arbor configuration. The
corresponding private SSH keys must remain on the laptop and must never be
uploaded to Git, the Nix store, the Registry, or another host.

## Install the upstream Windows service

Download the current approved upstream Yggdrasil Windows MSI from the official
installation page, verify its provenance and checksum according to the
operator's release process, and install it locally. Do not paste a private
key, generated config containing private material, or an Arbor credential into
chat, Git, or a command line.

Official references:

- [Yggdrasil Windows installation](https://yggdrasil-network.github.io/installation-windows.html)
- [Yggdrasil configuration](https://yggdrasil-network.github.io/configuration.html)

Run PowerShell as Administrator for installation and service management:

```powershell
$MsiPath = "C:\Users\<operator>\Downloads\yggdrasil-<approved-version>-x64.msi"
Start-Process msiexec.exe -Wait -ArgumentList @('/i', $MsiPath, '/qn')
Get-Service -Name yggdrasil
```

Use the architecture and version approved for the laptop. Keep the persistent
identity generated by the installation. Do not use Yggdrasil autoconfiguration
for this enrollment if it would regenerate the node identity or address.

## Generate and install the static public-peer configuration

Have the Arbor operator or an approved export tool produce the Windows
configuration from the accepted public metadata. The resulting file must
contain only the approved public peer information and the persistent local
identity settings needed by Yggdrasil. It must preserve the exact pinned
public keys and `AllowedPublicKeys` policy from the accepted records.

Do not hand-maintain a guessed cluster peer list. Do not copy a NixOS
provider-socket configuration to Windows: the Unix socket and Arbor Network
Manager convergence contract do not exist on this client.

After reviewing the generated file for the expected snapshot/generation and
for absence of Arbor credentials, install it using the path documented by the
current upstream MSI. A typical explicitly selected path is shown below; use
the actual service configuration path reported by the installed version:

```powershell
$ConfigPath = "$env:ProgramData\Yggdrasil\yggdrasil.conf"
$ApprovedConfig = "C:\Users\<operator>\Downloads\yggdrasil-approved.conf"
Copy-Item -LiteralPath $ApprovedConfig -Destination $ConfigPath -Force

Restart-Service -Name yggdrasil
Get-Service -Name yggdrasil | Select-Object Name, Status, StartType
```

Restrict the configuration file and its containing directory to the operator
and SYSTEM/Administrators using the Windows ACLs appropriate for the installed
service. The local Yggdrasil private key is runtime secret material; never
include it in the exported public metadata or commit it anywhere.

## Verify the local Yggdrasil service

Use the installed `yggdrasilctl` executable. If it is not on `PATH`, resolve
its path from the MSI installation rather than downloading an unrelated copy.
These commands are checks only; they do not enroll the laptop or authorize it:

```powershell
$YggCtl = "C:\Program Files\Yggdrasil\yggdrasilctl.exe"
& $YggCtl getSelf
& $YggCtl getPeers
Get-Service -Name yggdrasil
```

Confirm that `getSelf` reports the persistent local public identity expected
for the enrollment record, and that `getPeers` shows only approved peers.
Record the public identity/fingerprint and observed peer names, but never
record private key material.

For each approved target, use its Registry-supplied Yggdrasil address rather
than a guessed address:

```powershell
$TargetYggAddress = "<address-from-accepted-registry-record>"
Test-NetConnection -ComputerName $TargetYggAddress -Port 22 -InformationLevel Detailed
Get-NetRoute -AddressFamily IPv6 | Sort-Object RouteMetric, InterfaceMetric
```

The TCP check is only transport evidence. It is not SSH authorization and is
not evidence of Arbor enrollment.

## Firewall cautions

Keep the Yggdrasil adapter and its firewall rules separate from public and LAN
interfaces. Review the effective rules before and after starting the service:

```powershell
Get-NetAdapter | Sort-Object Name | Format-Table Name, Status, InterfaceDescription
Get-NetFirewallProfile | Format-Table Name, Enabled, DefaultInboundAction, DefaultOutboundAction
Get-NetFirewallRule -PolicyStore ActiveStore |
  Where-Object Enabled -eq 'True' |
  Select-Object DisplayName, Direction, Action, Profile, InterfaceType
```

Do not enable broad inbound SSH, WinRM, SMB, or RDP access on the Yggdrasil,
Wi-Fi, Ethernet, or public profiles merely to make testing pass. Permit only
the explicitly required operator path and approved source identities. A
reachable private overlay does not authorize service exposure on arbitrary
physical interfaces. Preserve the public/bootstrap path independently of
Yggdrasil convergence.

## Bootstrap SSH verification

The laptop must retain ordinary bootstrap SSH access, whether or not its
Yggdrasil enrollment is complete:

- laptop -> `r640-0`
- laptop -> `desktoptoodle`
- laptop -> `eVolver`

Use each supplied laptop private key locally with `IdentitiesOnly`; never copy
either private key to a target. Replace only the placeholders below with the
operator's existing local paths and the approved bootstrap names/addresses:

```powershell
$SshOptions = @(
  '-o', 'BatchMode=yes',
  '-o', 'IdentitiesOnly=yes',
  '-o', 'ConnectTimeout=10'
)
$LaptopKey = "C:\Users\<operator>\.ssh\<existing-private-key>"

ssh @SshOptions -i $LaptopKey ash@<r640-0-bootstrap-host> hostname
ssh @SshOptions -i $LaptopKey ash@<desktoptoodle-bootstrap-host> hostname
ssh @SshOptions -i $LaptopKey ash@<eVolver-bootstrap-host> hostname
```

Repeat with the second local key if the operator needs to establish which
credential succeeds on each path. Record only the key label, target, remote
account, hostname, and route. Do not print private paths or key contents in a
shared report. The expected target-side authorization labels are the
repository's `laptopOperatorKeys` set; physical success is currently
**pending** and must not be inferred from configuration evaluation.

## Private-Ygg and Arbor-route verification

After the accepted metadata is installed and `getPeers` shows convergence,
verify transport to all three NixOS participants:

```powershell
Test-NetConnection -ComputerName <r640-0-ygg-address> -Port 22
Test-NetConnection -ComputerName <desktoptoodle-ygg-address> -Port 22
Test-NetConnection -ComputerName <eVolver-ygg-address> -Port 22

ssh @SshOptions -i $LaptopKey ash@<r640-0-ygg-address> hostname
ssh @SshOptions -i $LaptopKey ash@<desktoptoodle-ygg-address> hostname
ssh @SshOptions -i $LaptopKey ash@<eVolver-ygg-address> hostname
```

Use the route/endpoint selected by the current Arbor route workflow where the
Windows operator tooling supports it. Otherwise record that the Windows
client used the approved static Ygg address and that Arbor route execution was
not available on Windows. Do not hard-code Ygg addresses into a permanent SSH
configuration as a substitute for accepted route metadata.

On the NixOS side, the corresponding checks must use `arbor-manager route ...`
and compare the selected provider/route with actual SSH results. A Ygg route
is usable transport only when the accepted Arbor policy and observed health
permit it; bootstrap/LAN fallback must remain available.

## Enrollment, refresh, and recovery

1. Submit the laptop's Yggdrasil public identity through the approved Arbor
   enrollment workflow, if external operator identities are supported. Submit
   public identity metadata only; do not submit the private Yggdrasil key.
2. Obtain a new accepted snapshot whenever peer membership, public keys,
   endpoints, capabilities, or revocation state changes.
3. Regenerate/reinstall the static Windows configuration from that accepted
   snapshot and verify the recorded generation/digest before restarting the
   service.
4. If a peer is revoked, its key changes, or the snapshot expires, stop using
   the affected route and refresh the configuration. Do not bypass
   `AllowedPublicKeys` or pin an unreviewed peer to restore connectivity.
5. If Yggdrasil is unavailable, use bootstrap SSH over the preserved public/LAN
   path. A Registry outage, sealed OpenBao instance, missing provider state, or
   empty Yggdrasil peer set must degrade connectivity without becoming a
   reason to grant new trust.

## Current verification record

This document is an onboarding procedure, not an acceptance result. No
Windows installation, Yggdrasil identity, peer convergence, firewall review,
Arbor route, or SSH path was verified by Codex.

| Path | Bootstrap SSH | Arbor route | Private Ygg | Verified |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Laptop -> `r640-0` | pending | pending/not available on Windows | pending | no |
| Laptop -> `desktoptoodle` | pending | pending/not available on Windows | pending | no |
| Laptop -> `eVolver` | pending | pending/not available on Windows | pending | no |

The NixOS participant paths remain a separate physical acceptance task:
`desktoptoodle -> r640-0`, `desktoptoodle -> eVolver`, and `r640-0 -> eVolver`.
This artifact does not claim any of them succeeded.

## Explicit Windows limitation

There is no Windows-compatible Arbor Network Manager/provider-socket
integration in this repository. Therefore this procedure cannot claim
generation-bound runtime peer convergence on Windows. It provides a pinned,
static, persistent Yggdrasil transport configuration derived from accepted
public Arbor metadata, with manual refresh/revocation checks. Registry remains
the trust authority; Yggdrasil remains transport; discovery never becomes
enrollment.
